page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this arm64 server features dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core, 64.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48571.1 and a passmark CPU score of 17314.07. The instance demonstrates solid capabilities in multi-threaded tasks, such as software compilation with clang, which scored 26063.0, and static web serving throughput at 33.11 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with geekbench single-core scores of 958.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.31 GB/sec falling into the lower performance tier.

The ARM-based architecture and dedicated physical cores offer a resource-dense profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded, scale-out workloads. The inclusion of 1900 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage makes this instance well-suited for database operations, web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation, while it is less optimal for workloads heavily reliant on single-threaded execution speed or x86-specific instruction sets.
